full_text_en:
Zhao Jun v. Xiang Huimin and He Xueqin — dispute over private lending

Ruling Summary

I. Where a spouse is suspected of malicious collusion with a third party and fabricating marital debts through false litigation, the unilateral admission of the debt by that spouse does not necessarily relieve the "lender" of its burden of proof regarding the establishment and validity of the loan relationship.

II. Where the spouse of the borrower does not participate in the litigation and neither the lender nor the borrower explicitly waives the debt share that the spouse may be liable for, in order to ascertain the facts of the case, the spouse of the borrower, who has a legal interest in the outcome of the case, shall be added as a third party to the litigation in accordance with the law, so as to form substantive adversarial proceedings.

III. Where the lender provides only an IOU to support the loan relationship, the court shall conduct an in-depth investigation of ancillary facts to determine the authenticity of the mutual agreement on lending, such as the necessity of incurring the debt and the reasonableness of the use of the funds. If the lender is unable to provide evidence to prove the delivery of the loan, the court shall comprehensively consider factors such as the lender's financial condition, the source of funds, the method of delivery, and witnesses present at the scene to assess the credibility of the parties' statements. For large loans where only an IOU exists without any evidence of delivery, and where the parties' statements contain significant doubts or contradictions, the court shall determine, based on the rules of evidence, that the "lender" has not fulfilled its burden of proof and shall render a judgment dismissing the claim.

Plaintiff: Zhao Jun, male, 45 years old, Han ethnicity, residing at Shuicheng Road, Changning District, Shanghai.

Defendant: Xiang Huimin, male, 44 years old, Han ethnicity, registered domicile: Zhuxi Town, Xianju County, Zhejiang Province; residing at Honggu Road, Changning District, Shanghai.

Defendant: He Xueqin, female, 39 years old, Han ethnicity, registered domicile: Zhuxi Town, Xianju County, Zhejiang Province; residing at Honggu Road, Changning District, Shanghai.

Plaintiff Zhao Jun filed an action with the Changning District People's Court of Shanghai due to a dispute over private lending with defendants Xiang Huimin and He Xueqin.

Plaintiff Zhao Jun alleged: The plaintiff and defendant Xiang Huimin are friends. On July 20, 2007, Xiang Huimin borrowed RMB 200,000 from the plaintiff on the grounds of decorating his house, with an agreed annual interest rate of 5% and a term of two years. On that day, the plaintiff took RMB 200,000 in cash from a safe at home, walked to the dry-cleaning store operated by Xiang Huimin, and delivered the loan to him; Xiang Huimin issued a receipt on the spot. On July 23, 2009, under the plaintiff's demand, Xiang Huimin paid interest of RMB 20,000 and requested an extension of the loan term for another two years. On July 27, 2011, the plaintiff again demanded repayment from Xiang Huimin, but he still failed to repay. The plaintiff believed that since the loan in this case was borrowed by Xiang Huimin from him, and the IOU and the demand notice were also signed and confirmed by Xiang Huimin, he only sued Xiang Huimin. As to whether defendant He Xueqin should bear joint repayment liability, the plaintiff did not express an opinion. The plaintiff requested the court to order Xiang Huimin to repay the loan of RMB 200,000 and to pay interest calculated at an annual rate of 5% on the principal of RMB 200,000 from July 23, 2009 until the date the judgment takes effect.

Defendant Xiang Huimin argued: He had no objection to the facts alleged by plaintiff Zhao Jun, but he was currently unable to repay the loan. As for the use of the borrowed funds, RMB 100,000 was used to decorate the house owned by the two defendants, and the other RMB 100,000 was used on August 2, 2007 to prepay the bank loan for the purchase of that house. Therefore, the loan in question was a marital joint debt and should be jointly repaid by the two defendants.

Defendant He Xueqin argued: First, the loan claimed by plaintiff Zhao Jun did not exist. In 2007, the two defendants had ample funds of their own and had no need to incur debt. The IOU provided by the plaintiff was forged by Xiang Huimin after the event; He Xueqin had already applied for forensic examination of the actual formation time of the IOU, but the examination could not be conducted due to lack of conditions. Moreover, the plaintiff did not have the financial capacity to lend RMB 200,000 at that time, and he did not provide any evidence of delivery of the loan. Second, He Xueqin was never aware of the loan claimed by the plaintiff. On June 18, 2009, the two defendants signed an agreement stating that any external debt would not be established unless both parties confirmed it. Therefore, even if the loan existed, it should be Xiang Huimin's personal debt. Third, the two defendants married on September 20, 2005 and began living separately in July 2010. He Xueqin filed for divorce on August 25, 2010 and May 12, 2011 respectively. In those two lawsuits, Xiang Huimin did not mention the loan in this case. Currently, the third divorce lawsuit between the two defendants is pending. However, in addition to the disputed debt in this case, two other creditors suddenly filed lawsuits in court demanding repayment. Clearly, this case is a false lawsuit initiated by the plaintiff and Xiang Huimin through malicious collusion in an attempt to transfer assets, and the two should be held legally liable.

The Changning District People's Court of Shanghai found the following facts upon trial:

Plaintiff Zhao Jun and defendant Xiang Huimin are friends. The two defendants are husband and wife, having registered their marriage on September 20, 2005. Xiang Huimin issued an IOU dated July 20, 2007 to the plaintiff, stating: "I, Xiang Huimin, borrow RMB 200,000 (two hundred thousand yuan) from Zhao Jun, to be repaid before July 20, 2009, with interest calculated at 5%." Xiang Huimin signed as the borrower at the foot of the IOU. Later, the plaintiff wrote a Payment Demand Notice stating: "Xiang Huimin borrowed RMB 200,000 (two hundred thousand yuan) from Zhao Jun, to be repaid before July 20, 2009, but the deadline has passed and it has not been repaid. This notice is to demand payment from Xiang Huimin." The notice was dated July 23, 2009. Xiang Huimin added a note on the notice: "I understand. Due to poor business operations, I have no money to repay. I request an extension of two years, with the same interest." Thereafter, the plaintiff wrote another Payment Demand Notice stating: "Xiang Huimin borrowed RMB 200,000 from Zhao Jun. After repeated demands, it has still not been repaid. This notice is to demand repayment of the loan and interest again." The notice was dated July 27, 2011. Xiang Huimin added a note on this notice: "Due to poor business operations, I have no money to repay. I request an extension of two years, with the same interest," and signed his name.

Further found, as of July 19, 2007, the balance in the bank account of defendant Xiang Huimin, account number 1001XXXXXXXXXXX3366 with the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China, was RMB 167,545.34. On August 2, 2007, Xiang Huimin withdrew RMB 100,000 from the said bank account. On the same day, Xiang Huimin repaid a personal housing loan of RMB 100,000 to the China Construction Bank.

Further found, on June 18, 2009, the two defendants signed an Agreement, confirming matters such as their business operations, property status, and housing loans, but the disputed loan in this case was not mentioned. The parties also agreed that "for other debts, any debt not confirmed by either party shall not be established." In July 2010, the two defendants began to live separately. On September 28, 2010 and June 1, 2011, He Xueqin filed divorce lawsuits against Xiang Huimin with the Changning District People's Court of Shanghai respectively. During the proceedings of the two lawsuits, Xiang Huimin did not mention the disputed loan in this case, and both divorce lawsuits were later mediated and resulted in no divorce. On August 31, 2012, He Xueqin filed a third lawsuit for divorce from Xiang Huimin, which is currently pending.

The above facts are confirmed by the following evidence: the IOU dated July 20, 2007 provided by plaintiff Zhao Jun; the Payment Demand Notice dated July 23, 2009; the Payment Demand Notice dated July 27, 2011; the China Construction Bank Individual Loan Repayment Receipt provided by defendant Xiang Huimin; the Agreement dated June 18, 2009 between the two defendants provided by defendant He Xueqin; the court mediation records of October 13, 2010 and June 1, 2011; the transaction records of the bank account of defendant Xiang Huimin, account number 1001XXXXXXXXXXX2009 with the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China, obtained ex officio by the Changning District People's Court of Shanghai; and the statements of the parties in court. These are sufficient for determination.

The disputed issues in this case are: whether the loan relationship between plaintiff Zhao Jun and defendant Xiang Huimin was established and valid, and, if so, whether defendant He Xueqin is liable for repayment.

The Changning District People's Court of Shanghai held at first instance: According to the rules of evidence in civil proceedings, in a contract dispute, the party claiming that a contractual relationship has been established and is valid bears the burden of proof for the facts of contract formation and validity. At the same time, according to the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, a loan contract between natural persons takes effect upon the lender's provision of the loan. Therefore, plaintiff Zhao Jun, claiming that a valid loan contract relationship exists between him and Xiang Huimin, must bear the burden of proving both the mutual agreement on the loan and the actual delivery of the loan. The plaintiff provided the IOU to prove the mutual agreement on the loan between him and Xiang Huimin. Regarding the delivery of the loan, the plaintiff claimed that he was not accustomed to using bank cards, so he kept large amounts of cash at home, and the RMB 200,000 was delivered in cash to Xiang Huimin in one lump sum. Defendant Xiang Huimin admitted the plaintiff's above claims and stated that after receiving the loan, he also kept it in cash and used RMB 100,000 of it on August 2, 2007 to prepay the housing loan. Defendant He Xueqin expressly denied the authenticity of the loan.

In this case, first, although plaintiff Zhao Jun initially claimed to seek repayment from Xiang Huimin, Xiang Huimin argued that the loan was used for the joint life of the two defendants and should be jointly repaid by both defendants. In fact, upon court investigation, in the third divorce lawsuit between the two defendants, Xiang Huimin consistently treated the loan in this case as a marital joint debt and requested He Xueqin to bear repayment liability. Since the outcome of this case is legally related to He Xueqin, the court lawfully added her as a third party to the proceedings. Later, due to Xiang Huimin's above defense, the plaintiff applied to add He Xueqin as a defendant. During this process, the plaintiff and Xiang Huimin repeatedly objected to He Xueqin's participation in this lawsuit, which not only lacked legal basis but also defied common sense. He Xueqin, as a defendant and an interested party in this case, is certainly entitled to state her opinions on the disputed loan and raise defenses.

Second, given the current marital status and conflict of interest between the two defendants, defendant Xiang Huimin's admission of the disputed loan cannot naturally give rise to the legal effect of both defendants' admission of the debt. Moreover, Xiang Huimin claimed that on August 2, 2007, he used RMB 100,000 of the loan to prepay the housing loan. However, upon the court's ex officio investigation, Xiang Huimin's bank transaction records showed that on that day, RMB 100,000 was withdrawn from his bank account, which corresponds to the repayment of his bank loan in terms of time and amount. In addition, Xiang Huimin's bank account had more than one hundred thousand yuan in deposits during the same period, and his housing loan from the bank enjoyed a 30% discount on the interest rate. Borrowing from others at an annual interest rate of 5% to offset the bank loan lacked necessity and reasonableness. When the court held a hearing on March 7, 2013, Xiang Huimin, having been properly summoned, explicitly refused to appear in court. The above facts and conduct are sufficient to cast doubt on the authenticity of Xiang Huimin's relevant statements. Therefore, for the above reasons, plaintiff Zhao Jun still bears the corresponding burden of proof to establish the existence and validity of the loan relationship between him and Xiang Huimin.

Third, plaintiff Zhao Jun stated that he owns multiple properties and is engaged in business activities, so he has the corresponding capacity to lend cash. However, he also stated that at the time of lending RMB 200,000 to Xiang Huimin, he himself was burdened with a huge bank loan for purchasing a house. Therefore, the court granted the plaintiff a reasonable period to provide evidence to prove his asset condition and cash lending capacity, and explained the legal consequences of failing to do so within the time limit. Subsequently, the plaintiff explicitly refused to provide the corresponding evidence. The court held that the plaintiff explicitly waived his right to continue adducing evidence, and the existing evidence he provided failed to prove the delivery of the loan or the plaintiff's own cash lending capacity. His account of the lending process was also inconsistent with common sense. Therefore, he must bear the legal consequences of failing to meet his burden of proof. The court does not support the plaintiff's claims in accordance with the law. As for Xiang Huimin's personal admission of the loan, since there is no dispute between him and the plaintiff on this matter, he may repay the plaintiff on his own; the court does not address this issue.

Accordingly, pursuant to Articles 196 and 210 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 144 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, and Articles 2 and 5 of the Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Evidence in Civil Proceedings, the Changning District People's Court of Shanghai rendered the following judgment on April 19, 2013:

All claims of plaintiff Zhao Jun are dismissed.

Court acceptance fee of RMB 4,300 shall be borne by plaintiff Zhao Jun.

After the first-instance judgment, neither party appealed, and the judgment has become legally effective.
